lines: Salesforce corporate development chief John Somorjai describes a disciplined build-partner-buy framework in which the best acquisitions speed up the product roadmap, bring in top talent and plug startups into Salesforce's distribution, including some 15,000 sales reps.

He argues distribution is the real shortcut: startups can spend years and heavy capital building global sales channels, which deals like Slack and the AI-native platform Finn bypass; Slack, he says, has become the conversational interface for enterprise AI agents.

Due diligence centers on security and data integrity, which he calls the top deal-breakers: a failed penetration test or weak control over customer contracts can sink a deal regardless of product quality, and ARR alone can mask customer attrition.

Somorjai expects a reckoning for non-generational startups on unsustainable valuations, since few buyers can absorb multi-billion-dollar deals, and sees software pricing shifting from per-seat to outcome-based.

Salesforce Ventures keeps a broad aperture, now including physical AI and robotics, to watch industry shifts and spot future targets, while integration focuses on retaining talent, with many acquired founders rising into senior leadership.
title: Inside Salesforce’s $100 Billion M&A Playbook | John Somorjai
